decisions.what: Owned the single embedder inside the scheduler worker; EpisodeServer and the ingestion loop now hold only a cloneable SchedulerHandle (bounded mpsc senders).
decisions.why: C4 requires one model instance and bounded scheduling rather than a second BGE model. Constructing LocalEmbedder once and moving it into the worker makes duplication structurally impossible in production.

decisions.what: Biased tokio::select! branch order is shutdown -> interactive -> ingest, with a shutdown borrow check also at the top of each loop iteration.
decisions.why: When not shutting down, a queued interactive (recall/remember) job is always selected before another ingest batch (AC5). Listing shutdown first guarantees that once cancellation is signaled, no further batch is started even if ingest jobs are already queued (AC6).

decisions.what: Worker awaits each spawn_blocking job to completion before selecting the next job (one active job at a time).
decisions.why: Preserves the one-model memory budget and makes fairness deterministic: an already-queued interactive job wins before the next ingest batch, while active spawn_blocking inference is never aborted (C5 — Tokio cannot cancel it).

decisions.what: Empty and over-max (>64) batches are rejected at the SchedulerHandle before any job is scheduled; the ingestion loop additionally partitions with Vec::chunks(INGEST_BATCH_MAX).
decisions.why: AC4 requires a defined bounded batch size and that empty batches do not invoke embedding. Handle-level guards make the contract enforceable and directly testable regardless of caller.

decisions.what: Added pure validate_batch_output (length + every-vector dimension) in the scheduler module and call it before per-item upsert; on mismatch the batch is skipped with structured namespace/batch context.
decisions.why: Design §3 batch contract: mismatches fail that batch and leave items eligible for the next reconcile. Placing the validator in the scheduler module keeps the batch contract with the scheduler and makes it unit-testable.

decisions.what: Retained per-item exists_source dedup and per-item upsert in run_ingestion_loop instead of switching to bulk.
decisions.why: Bulk DB dedup/upsert is explicitly owned by the dependent task tk-252520f7698a; this task scopes to the scheduler + lifecycle only. Embedding is now bounded/batched; persistence batching is deferred.

decisions.what: Barrier-based recorder tests use #[tokio::test(flavor = "multi_thread", worker_threads = 2)].
decisions.why: They block the test thread on a std::sync::mpsc recv to observe the active embedder. On the default current_thread runtime that single-thread block deadlocked (the worker could not run); multi_thread lets the spawned worker progress on another thread and also better reflects the #[tokio::main] production runtime. Documented inline.

decisions.what: Wrapped each receiver in Option and introduced a Sel enum (Shutdown / InteractiveClosed / IngestClosed / Job); each select arm is guarded by `if <rx>.is_some()`.
decisions.why: A closed mpsc::Receiver returns None from recv() immediately and is therefore always ready. Leaving it in a biased select either spins or — as in the reported bug — maps to a loop exit that starves/abandons the other queue. The guard removes a closed channel from polling; the worker keeps servicing the open queue and exits only on shutdown or when both are closed. This is the structural fix the review asked for.

decisions.what: Added two barrier/yield-driven regression tests (one per channel direction) that drive run_worker directly with separately controlled senders.
decisions.why: The bug only manifests when one sender class disappears while the other still has work. Dropping one sender in the test reproduces it deterministically: on the old code the surviving queue's job never starts (or its send fails), so the tests fail; on the fixed code they pass. Covering both directions pins the symmetric fix.

decisions.what: Used the multi_thread flavor for the new tests (and kept it on the prior barrier tests).
decisions.why: They block the test thread on a std::sync::mpsc recv / rely on the worker making progress independently; the default current_thread runtime deadlocks, as established in attempt 1.

subagent_reports.topic: Episode resilience: sqlx pool lifecycle, Tokio graceful cancellation + bounded concurrency, fastembed batch API — discovery opportunity scout + architecture validation

sources.label: SQLx PoolOptions (docs.rs, canonical)
sources.summary: acquire_timeout caps total Pool::acquire() wait across semaphore+liveness-test+connect phases; test_before_acquire defaults true (pings idle conn, can disable + use before_acquire for age-gated ping); max_lifetime non-infinite recommended (retire conns to let PG clean parse trees/caches); idle_timeout closes idle conns; min_connections warms pool and is best-effort with a deadline. connect() opens at least max(1,min_connections).

sources.label: SQLx PgPoolOptions (docs.rs)
sources.summary: new() = sane light-duty default; production should set max_connections. acquire_slow_threshold/acquire_time_level give pool-acquire observability without code changes.

sources.label: fastembed-rs TextEmbedding::embed API reference
sources.summary: embed(texts, batch_size: Option<usize>) takes a batch and returns Vec<Embedding>; default batch size 256; tokenization is parallelized across inputs internally. Current per-item embed_one loop defeats built-in batching + internal parallelism.

sources.label: Tokio JoinHandle::abort / AbortHandle (docs.rs)
sources.summary: abort() cancels an async task (cancellation may lag; is_finished can be false post-abort). CRITICAL: spawn_blocking tasks (the fastembed embed call) CANNOT be aborted — abort is a no-op once running. Graceful shutdown must be cooperative for the ingestion worker, not abort-based.

sources.label: Tokio select! cancellation safety (docs.rs)
sources.summary: select! in a loop requires cancel-safe branches; dropping an unfinished future must be a no-op. Recommended graceful-shutdown shape: select! { _ = shutdown.cancelled/changed() => break, _ = tick/work => {} }.

subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Proposal scope is well-aligned with canonical Rust/Tokio/SQLx best practice; deviations are all in the CURRENT code, not the proposed direction. (1) store.rs connect() uses only max_connections — no acquire_timeout/idle_timeout/max_lifetime/min_connections, so 'bounded pool lifecycle' is a real, doc-backed gap; note SQLx already defaults acquire_timeout (~30s) and test_before_acquire=true, so bounding is about making limits explicit + adding retirement, not fixing an unbounded-hang. (2) embed.rs Mutex<TextEmbedding> serializes recall/remember/ingest, and lib.rs run_ingestion_loop calls embed_one per item inside spawn_blocking — double anti-pattern: it discards fastembed's native batch API (batch_size default 256) AND its internal tokenization parallelism, and holds the single embedder mutex once per item, maximally starving interactive recall. Batching ingestion into one embed(Vec<String>) call per flush is the by-the-book fix. (3) lib.rs spawns the ingestion loop detached (tokio::spawn, handle dropped) with no shutdown ownership; graceful cancellation is doc-supported but has a sharp edge: the embed step runs in spawn_blocking which JoinHandle::abort CANNOT stop — shutdown MUST be cooperative (check a cancellation signal between batches / via select!), not abort-based. tokio-util (CancellationToken) is NOT currently a dependency; a watch/Notify-based signal avoids adding a dep, or add tokio-util deliberately. (4) config.rs silently falls back on every invalid value (pool_size, interval) and silently drops malformed EPISODE_PROJECT_ROOTS entries (split_once('=') -> None -> filtered) — matches the 'deterministic validation + report rejected entries' scope; boring fix is typed parse returning Result with per-entry diagnostics.

validation.notes: Proposed direction is validated against canonical docs for all three researched surfaces. No blockers. Edge cases the design phase must pin down, not blockers: (a) spawn_blocking is un-abortable => cooperative shutdown only; (b) fastembed batch embed keeps ordering (Vec<Embedding> 1:1 with inputs) so batch upsert can zip inputs+embeddings — verify empty-batch and dim-check paths; (c) bounding recall/ingest contention should prefer a SEPARATE embedder instance or a bounded worker for ingestion rather than sharing the one recall-serving mutex, else batching still blocks recall during a large flush; (d) namespace-required manual-only forget is a store-layer predicate change (DELETE ... WHERE id=$1 AND namespace=$2 AND source='manual') — structurally correct per P33, keep it in SQL not app logic.

tradeoffs: Explicit pool limits (acquire_timeout/idle_timeout/max_lifetime/min_connections) add config surface + env docs but make failure modes deterministic and observable; SQLx already applies sane defaults so under-tuning is safe.

Batching ingestion embeds (one embed() per flush) massively cuts per-item mutex churn and model-call overhead, but a very large single batch increases peak memory and one long blocking call; mitigate with a bounded flush size (not the full backlog) rather than default 256-cap reliance.

Cooperative graceful shutdown (watch/Notify/select! or tokio-util CancellationToken) adds a small amount of lifecycle plumbing but is the only correct option because the embed step is spawn_blocking and cannot be aborted.

Separating the ingestion embedder from the recall embedder removes recall starvation but doubles model memory (~one extra BGE-large instance); a bounded single-worker ingest queue is the lighter-weight alternative that keeps one model.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep abort()-based shutdown on the ingestion JoinHandle
alternatives_considered.rationale: JoinHandle::abort is a no-op on the running spawn_blocking embed task (Tokio docs); it cannot guarantee clean shutdown and risks tearing down mid-DB-write. Cooperative cancellation between batches is required.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep per-item embed_one loop but drop the mutex hold time
alternatives_considered.rationale: Defeats fastembed's native batch API + internal tokenization parallelism (batch_size default 256); batch embed per flush is both simpler and faster and is the documented usage.

alternatives_considered.option: Add tokio-util CancellationToken dependency for shutdown
alternatives_considered.rationale: Idiomatic and clean, but tokio-util is not yet a dep; a tokio::sync::watch or Notify signal already in-tree achieves cooperative cancellation with zero new deps. Design phase should pick one explicitly — either is acceptable; avoid inventing an ad-hoc AtomicBool poll.

alternatives_considered.option: Enforce namespace/manual-only forget in application code
alternatives_considered.rationale: P33 structural-correctness: encode the constraint in the DELETE predicate (id + namespace + source='manual') so ingested rows are undeletable via the tool regardless of caller, not via a Rust guard that can be bypassed.

architecture_judgement.recommendation: Proceed to design. Anchor design on: (1) explicit PgPoolOptions bounds (acquire_timeout, idle_timeout, max_lifetime, optional min_connections) with values surfaced as documented env vars; (2) batch ingestion via one fastembed embed(Vec<String>) per bounded flush + batch upsert (zip inputs:embeddings, ordering guaranteed), and isolate ingestion embedding from recall (bounded ingest worker or separate embedder) so recall is not starved; (3) cooperative graceful shutdown for the owned ingestion task using an in-tree watch/Notify signal + select! (NOT abort — embed is spawn_blocking); (4) typed config validation returning Result with per-entry rejected-root diagnostics; (5) store-layer namespace-required, source='manual' forget predicate. All five are boring, doc-backed, and structurally enforced.

subagent_reports.recommendation: Proceed to design with the five anchors above. No architectural blockers; the proposed direction matches canonical SQLx/Tokio/fastembed usage. The single sharpest edge to encode explicitly in design.md: ingestion embedding runs in spawn_blocking and is un-abortable, so shutdown must be cooperative and recall/ingest isolation must be real (separate embedder or bounded worker) not just batched.
follow_ups: Design must decide tokio-util CancellationToken vs in-tree watch/Notify for shutdown signalling.
Design must set a bounded ingest flush size rather than relying on fastembed's 256 default to cap peak memory.

Cargo.toml dependency hygiene: proposal claims unused deps (e.g. notify present but ingestion loop is interval-poll, not notify-driven) + Voyage backend advertised-but-unimplemented — verify and reconcile capability signaling in a design task.

decisions.what: Wrapped each receiver in Option and introduced a Sel enum (Shutdown / InteractiveClosed / IngestClosed / Job); each select arm is guarded by `if <rx>.is_some()`.
decisions.why: A closed mpsc::Receiver returns None from recv() immediately and is therefore always ready. Leaving it in a biased select either spins or — as in the reported bug — maps to a loop exit that starves/abandons the other queue. The guard removes a closed channel from polling; the worker keeps servicing the open queue and exits only on shutdown or when both are closed. This is the structural fix the review asked for.

decisions.what: Added two barrier/yield-driven regression tests (one per channel direction) that drive run_worker directly with separately controlled senders.
decisions.why: The bug only manifests when one sender class disappears while the other still has work. Dropping one sender in the test reproduces it deterministically: on the old code the surviving queue's job never starts (or its send fails), so the tests fail; on the fixed code they pass. Covering both directions pins the symmetric fix.

decisions.what: Used the multi_thread flavor for the new tests (and kept it on the prior barrier tests).
decisions.why: They block the test thread on a std::sync::mpsc recv / rely on the worker making progress independently; the default current_thread runtime deadlocks, as established in attempt 1.

items.text: `forget` requires `namespace`; its persistence operation deletes only a matching `source = 'manual'` row in that namespace. Wrong namespace, ingested source, unknown id, and repeated deletion return `removed: 0`.
Invalid or zero pool size/ingest interval, unknown embedding backend, and malformed/empty project-root entries cause startup validation to fail with the offending input name and expected format.
The SQLx pool config sets finite acquire, idle, and maximum-lifetime bounds. An unavailable database returns an acquisition error within the configured acquire limit.
Ingestion uses a defined bounded batch size. With at least 65 eligible memories, it makes multiple batches rather than one unbounded call.

## Why

Episode provides working local semantic recall, but must safely serve multiple local agent sessions and retain reliable behavior under malformed configuration, database stalls, ingest load, and process shutdown.

## Scope

- Require a namespace for deletion and permit deletion only of manually created memories; ingested ADV wisdom/reflections remain protected.
- Validate all operator-facing configuration deterministically.
- Bound database-pool acquisition and connection lifetime behavior.
- Replace per-item ingestion work with bounded batching and prioritize interactive recall between ingestion batches.
- Give the ingestion worker an owned lifecycle and cooperative graceful shutdown path.
- Expand unit and integration coverage across config, MCP namespace semantics, store behavior, embedding contracts, and ingestion lifecycle.
- Reconcile backend capability signaling, environment documentation, dependency hygiene, CI advisory checks, release profile settings, and README behavior claims.

## Out of scope

- Network-exposed multi-tenant auth or external deletion-token management.
- Replacing pgvector, Rust, or the local embedding model.
- Unrelated memory features such as export or UI.

## Expected outcome

A local Episode deployment rejects unsafe configuration, protects cross-namespace and ingested memories from accidental deletion, handles bounded database failures, ingests efficiently without starving interactive recall, shuts down cleanly, and proves these properties with automated tests.

Observed problems:
- `forget(id)` has no namespace or source-class constraint.
- Configuration silently falls back for invalid values and malformed project-root entries.
- The database pool has no bounded acquisition or lifecycle policy.
- A single embedding mutex serializes recall, remember, and ingestion; ingestion also performs per-item dedup/embed/upsert work.
- The background ingestion task is detached and lacks graceful shutdown ownership.
- Key server, store, embedder, and configuration behavior lacks direct test coverage.
- The configured Voyage backend is advertised but intentionally unimplemented; unused dependencies and undocumented tuning variables add confusion.

This follow-up makes those boundaries explicit, observable, tested, and operationally bounded without changing Episode's purpose as a local persistent decision-memory MCP server.

# Design: Improve Episode resilience

## Architecture

Keep Episode local, single-model, and PostgreSQL-backed. Replace implicit trust and lifecycle behavior with typed inputs, SQL predicates, bounded worker queues, and owned shutdown handles.

## 1. Protected deletion

- `ForgetParams` gains required `namespace`.
- Replace `Store::forget(id)` with `Store::forget_manual(id, namespace)`.
- Store executes one SQL statement:
  `DELETE FROM memories WHERE id = $1 AND namespace = $2 AND source = 'manual'`.
- `removed` remains the response signal. The service never performs a pre-read or app-layer source check.
- README calls this restricted hard deletion, not soft removal.

## 2. Deterministic configuration and pool policy

- Parse `EPISODE_DB_POOL_SIZE` and `EPISODE_INGEST_INTERVAL_SECS` as non-zero bounded integers; invalid inputs return `Config::from_env()` errors naming the variable and expected form.
- Parse `EPISODE_EMBED_BACKEND` as an explicit enum. `local` is supported. `voyage` and unknown values fail validation as unsupported rather than starting then aborting later.
- Parse every `EPISODE_PROJECT_ROOTS` entry as non-empty `namespace=absolute-or-relative-path`; any malformed entry fails validation with its entry text.
- Configure `PgPoolOptions` with explicit constants: acquire timeout 5 seconds, idle timeout 10 minutes, max lifetime 30 minutes, current configured maximum connections, and `test_before_acquire(true)`.
- Keep eager database connection and migrations at startup. Prove the configured acquisition bound with an unreachable test endpoint wrapped in a deterministic timeout; do not change startup semantics solely for a test seam.
- Document supported variables and supported local-only embedding backend in `.env.example` and README.

## 3. Bounded priority embedding scheduler

- Introduce a scheduler owning the existing single local embedder.
- Accept two typed job classes through bounded channels: interactive (`recall`/`remember`, one text) and ingestion (one bounded batch).
- Scheduler uses biased selection and an injected execution recorder in tests: after an active batch finishes, it selects queued interactive work before another ingestion batch.
- Each selected job invokes the existing synchronous embedder in `spawn_blocking`; the scheduler awaits completion before selecting another job. This preserves the one-model memory budget and makes fairness deterministic: one active batch may finish, but an already queued interactive job wins before the next ingest batch.
- Ingestion batch maximum is 64 items. Empty batches do not invoke the scheduler.
- Batch output length and every vector dimension are validated before persistence; mismatches fail that batch and emit structured error context.

## 4. Batched ingestion and persistence

- For each project root, parse both ADV sources, collect stable source ids, and query existing ids in bulk. Preserve the existing source ids—including exploded reflection children—through the batch path.
- Partition remaining items into batches of at most 64.
- Submit one batch embedding job per partition; zip input and embedding output in stable order.
- Persist each completed partition through a transaction and static SQL/`QueryBuilder` binds; never construct mutation SQL with string formatting.
- A failed partition logs its namespace and leaves later partitions eligible for the next reconcile.
- The loop yields at each batch boundary; it never starts another ingestion batch ahead of queued interactive work.

## 5. Cooperative lifecycle

- `run()` creates an in-tree `tokio::sync::watch` shutdown signal and retains the ingestion `JoinHandle`.
- `run_ingestion_loop` uses cancellation-aware `select!` before waiting for the next interval and before beginning each batch. It does not attempt `JoinHandle::abort` for active `spawn_blocking` inference.
- After stdio service completion, `run()` signals shutdown and awaits ingestion task termination. Active embedding may finish; no subsequent batch begins.
- Scheduler shutdown closes ingestion intake after cancellation and exits after the active job returns. Interactive requests are not accepted during process teardown.

## 6. Verification and hygiene

- Unit tests: config table cases; deletion SQL predicate behavior; scheduler priority/order via recorder; empty/error batch behavior; cancellation boundaries.
- Integration tests: manual deletion succeeds only in matching namespace; ingested deletion is protected; bulk dedup/upsert; bounded batches; eager connection to unreachable endpoint exits within the configured bound.
- CI: retain existing format/clippy/build/test workflow and add a locked dependency advisory check with a repository-defined tool/action.
- Remove `notify` and `thiserror` if no shipped code uses them. Add explicit release profile settings after measuring build output.

## Independent validator result

`adv-researcher` validation: CAUTION, high confidence, no contract conflict.

Resolved before planning:
- Scheduler includes an observable execution-order seam for AC5.
- Pool acquisition proof uses eager-connect behavior, an unreachable endpoint, and deterministic timeout; startup remains eager.
- Existing CI is extended rather than replaced.
- Batch mutations use static SQL/`QueryBuilder` bindings and a transaction.

## Alternatives rejected

| Alternative | Reason |
|---|---|
| App-layer deletion guard | SQL predicate is the structural enforcement boundary. |
| Second BGE model for ingestion | Doubles model memory. |
| Unbounded/default-size ingestion batch | Weak peak-memory and fairness control. |
| `JoinHandle::abort` shutdown | Tokio cannot abort a running `spawn_blocking` task. |
| Leaving Voyage selectable | Advertises unavailable behavior. |

## Risks and mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|---|---|
| Active batch delays recall | Maximum 64-item batch; interactive jobs win before next batch. |
| Batch persistence fails partly | Transaction per batch; remaining work reappears on next reconcile. |
| Shutdown during inference | Cooperative stop after active job returns; no next batch. |
| Config migration breaks deployment | Document exact accepted values; validate existing Vision environment in tests/manual verification. |

## Contract mapping

- AC1: protected deletion.
- AC2: deterministic config parsing.
- AC3: explicit pool limits plus bounded eager-connect proof.
- AC4-AC5: 64-item batch scheduler and recorded interactive priority.
- AC6: owned cooperative lifecycle.
- AC7-AC8: tests, CI, docs, dependency/profile cleanup.

# Agreement: Improve Episode resilience

Approved by user on 2026-07-10.

## Objectives

1. Protect manual and ingested memory integrity.
2. Reject invalid runtime configuration deterministically.
3. Bound database and ingestion resource behavior.
4. Keep recall responsive during ingestion.
5. Prove behavior and align documentation/CI with shipped semantics.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `forget` requires `namespace`; its persistence operation deletes only a matching `source = 'manual'` row in that namespace. Wrong namespace, ingested source, unknown id, and repeated deletion return `removed: 0`.
2. Invalid or zero pool size/ingest interval, unknown embedding backend, and malformed/empty project-root entries cause startup validation to fail with the offending input name and expected format.
3. The SQLx pool config sets finite acquire, idle, and maximum-lifetime bounds. An unavailable database returns an acquisition error within the configured acquire limit.
4. Ingestion uses a defined bounded batch size. With at least 65 eligible memories, it makes multiple batches rather than one unbounded call.
5. If recall queues during ingest, it is selected before the next ingestion batch begins.
6. Shutdown is cooperative: after active work returns, no new batch starts and the owned ingestion task exits before process completion.
7. Automated tests cover deletion namespace/source behavior, config validation, pool/store behavior, batching, recall fairness, and shutdown. Format, clippy, build, and tests pass.
8. README and environment documentation accurately describe manual-only hard deletion, periodic ingestion, and unsupported Voyage behavior. CI includes dependency advisory checking; unused dependencies are removed and release profile settings are explicit.

## Constraints

- Local MCP service only; no network-exposed multi-tenant authorization.
- Retain Rust, pgvector, and BGE local embeddings.
- Use SQL predicates for deletion enforcement.
- Keep one model instance; use bounded scheduling rather than a second BGE instance.
- Use cooperative cancellation; do not rely on aborting active `spawn_blocking` inference.

## Avoidances

- App-layer-only deletion authorization.
- Silent configuration fallbacks.
- Unbounded ingestion batches.
- New export, UI, or unrelated memory-product scope.

## Evidence basis

- Episode full-repository review, 2026-07-10.
- Official SQLx `PoolOptions`, Tokio `JoinHandle`/`select!`, and FastEmbed batch API research collected during discovery.
